audit_status.source_base: Greek Philippians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for warning, confidence in flesh, loss/gain, knowing Messiah, righteousness from trust, pressing toward goal, heavenly citizenship.

verses.restored: Finally, my siblings, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you is not troublesome for me, and for you it is safe.

familiar.text: Finally, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not grievous, but for you it is safe.

modern.text: Finally, my brothers, rejoice in the Lord. It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you again, and it is a safeguard for you.

original.text: Τὸ λοιπόν, ἀδελφοί μου, χαίρετε ἐν κυρίῳ. τὰ αὐτὰ γράφειν ὑμῖν ἐμοὶ μὲν οὐκ ὀκνηρόν, ὑμῖν δὲ ἀσφαλές.

verses.restored: Watch the dogs; watch the harmful workers; watch the mutilation.

familiar.text: Beware of dogs, beware of evil workers, beware of the concision.

modern.text: Watch out for those dogs, those workers of evil, those mutilators of the flesh!

original.text: Βλέπετε τοὺς κύνας, βλέπετε τοὺς κακοὺς ἐργάτας, βλέπετε τὴν κατατομήν.

verses.restored: For we are the circumcision, the ones serving by Spirit of the Divine and boasting in Messiah Jesus and not having confidence in flesh,

familiar.text: For we are the circumcision, which worship God in the spirit, and rejoice in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh.

modern.text: For it is we who are the circumcision, we who worship by the Spirit of God, who glory in Christ Jesus, and who put no confidence in the flesh—

original.text: ἡμεῖς γάρ ἐσμεν ἡ περιτομή, οἱ πνεύματι θεοῦ λατρεύοντες καὶ καυχώμενοι ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐν σαρκὶ πεποιθότες,

verses.restored: though I myself have confidence even in flesh. If any other thinks to have confidence in flesh, I more:

familiar.text: Though I might also have confidence in the flesh. If any other man thinketh that he hath whereof he might trust in the flesh, I more:

modern.text: though I myself could have such confidence. If anyone else thinks he has grounds for confidence in the flesh, I have more:

original.text: καίπερ ἐγὼ ἔχων πεποίθησιν καὶ ἐν σαρκί. Εἴ τις δοκεῖ ἄλλος πεποιθέναι ἐν σαρκί, ἐγὼ μᾶλλον·

verses.restored: circumcised on the eighth day, from the race of Israel, tribe of Benjamin, Hebrew of Hebrews; according to Law, Pharisee;

familiar.text: Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews; as touching the law, a Pharisee;

modern.text: circumcised on the eighth day, of the people of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin; a Hebrew of Hebrews; as to the law, a Pharisee;

original.text: περιτομῇ ὀκταήμερος, ἐκ γένους Ἰσραήλ, φυλῆς Βενιαμίν, Ἑβραῖος ἐξ Ἑβραίων, κατὰ νόμον Φαρισαῖος,

verses.restored: according to zeal, pursuing/persecuting the assembly; according to righteousness/justice in Law, having become blameless.

familiar.text: Concerning zeal, persecuting the church; touching the righteousness which is in the law, blameless.

modern.text: as to zeal, persecuting the church; as to righteousness in the law, faultless.

original.text: κατὰ ⸀ζῆλος διώκων τὴν ἐκκλησίαν, κατὰ δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐν νόμῳ γενόμενος ἄμεμπτος.

verses.restored: But whatever things were gains to me, these I have considered loss because of Messiah.

familiar.text: But what things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ.

modern.text: But whatever was gain to me I count as loss for the sake of Christ.

original.text: Ἀλλὰ ἅτινα ἦν μοι κέρδη, ταῦτα ἥγημαι διὰ τὸν Χριστὸν ζημίαν.

verses.restored: Indeed therefore I also consider all things to be loss because of the surpassing value of the knowledge of Messiah Jesus my Lord, because of whom I lost all things and consider them refuse, so that I may gain Messiah

familiar.text: Yea doubtless, and I count all things but loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but dung, that I may win Christ,

modern.text: More than that, I count all things as loss compared to the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have lost all things. I consider them rubbish, that I may gain Christ

original.text: ἀλλὰ ⸀μενοῦνγε καὶ ἡγοῦμαι πάντα ζημίαν εἶναι διὰ τὸ ὑπερέχον τῆς γνώσεως Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ κυρίου μου διʼ ὃν τὰ πάντα ἐζημιώθην, καὶ ἡγοῦμαι ⸀σκύβαλα ἵνα Χριστὸν κερδήσω

verses.restored: and be found in him, not having my own righteousness/justice from Law, but that through trust/faithfulness of Messiah, the righteousness/justice from the Divine upon trust,

familiar.text: And be found in him, not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is of God by faith:

modern.text: and be found in Him, not having my own righteousness from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God on the basis of faith.

original.text: καὶ εὑρεθῶ ἐν αὐτῷ, μὴ ἔχων ἐμὴν δικαιοσύνην τὴν ἐκ νόμου ἀλλὰ τὴν διὰ πίστεως Χριστοῦ, τὴν ἐκ θεοῦ δικαιοσύνην ἐπὶ τῇ πίστει,

verses.restored: to know him and the power of his resurrection and the fellowship/participation of his sufferings, being conformed to his death,

familiar.text: That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable unto his death;

modern.text: I want to know Christ and the power of His resurrection and the fellowship of His sufferings, being conformed to Him in His death,

original.text: τοῦ γνῶναι αὐτὸν καὶ τὴν δύναμιν τῆς ἀναστάσεως αὐτοῦ καὶ ⸀κοινωνίαν παθημάτων αὐτοῦ, ⸀συμμορφιζόμενος τῷ θανάτῳ αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: if somehow I may arrive into the resurrection from the dead.

familiar.text: If by any means I might attain unto the resurrection of the dead.

modern.text: and so, somehow, to attain to the resurrection from the dead. Pressing on toward the Goal

original.text: εἴ πως καταντήσω εἰς τὴν ἐξανάστασιν ⸂τὴν ἐκ⸃ νεκρῶν.

verses.restored: Not that I already received or already have been made complete, but I pursue, if indeed I may take hold of that for which I also was taken hold of by Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: Not as though I had already attained, either were already perfect: but I follow after, if that I may apprehend that for which also I am apprehended of Christ Jesus.

modern.text: Not that I have already obtained all this, or have already been made perfect, but I press on to take hold of that for which Christ Jesus took hold of me.

original.text: Οὐχ ὅτι ἤδη ἔλαβον ἢ ἤδη τετελείωμαι, διώκω δὲ εἰ καὶ καταλάβω, ἐφʼ ᾧ καὶ κατελήμφθην ὑπὸ ⸀Χριστοῦ.

verses.restored: Siblings, I do not calculate myself to have taken hold; but one thing: forgetting the things behind and stretching forward to the things ahead,

familiar.text: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before,

modern.text: Brothers, I do not consider myself yet to have taken hold of it. But one thing I do: Forgetting what is behind and straining toward what is ahead,

original.text: ἀδελφοί, ἐγὼ ἐμαυτὸν ⸀οὐ λογίζομαι κατειληφέναι· ἓν δέ, τὰ μὲν ὀπίσω ἐπιλανθανόμενος τοῖς δὲ ἔμπροσθεν ἐπεκτεινόμενος,

verses.restored: I pursue toward the goal for the prize of the upward calling of the Divine in Messiah Jesus.

familiar.text: I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.

modern.text: I press on toward the goal to win the prize of God’s heavenly calling in Christ Jesus.

original.text: κατὰ σκοπὸν διώκω ⸀εἰς τὸ βραβεῖον τῆς ἄνω κλήσεως τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: Therefore, as many as are mature/complete, let us think this; and if in anything you think otherwise, this also the Divine will unveil to you.

familiar.text: Let us therefore, as many as be perfect, be thus minded: and if in any thing ye be otherwise minded, God shall reveal even this unto you.

modern.text: All of us who are mature should embrace this point of view. And if you think differently about some issue, God will reveal this to you as well.

original.text: ὅσοι οὖν τέλειοι, τοῦτο φρονῶμεν· καὶ εἴ τι ἑτέρως φρονεῖτε, καὶ τοῦτο ὁ θεὸς ὑμῖν ἀποκαλύψει·

verses.restored: Only, to what we have reached, walk in line by the same.

familiar.text: Nevertheless, whereto we have already attained, let us walk by the same rule, let us mind the same thing.

modern.text: Nevertheless, we must live up to what we have already attained. Citizenship in Heaven

original.text: πλὴν εἰς ὃ ἐφθάσαμεν, τῷ αὐτῷ ⸀στοιχεῖν.

verses.restored: Become co-imitators of me, siblings, and watch those walking this way, just as you have us as pattern.

familiar.text: Brethren, be followers together of me, and mark them which walk so as ye have us for an ensample.

modern.text: Join one another in following my example, brothers, and carefully observe those who walk according to the pattern we set for you.

original.text: Συμμιμηταί μου γίνεσθε, ἀδελφοί, καὶ σκοπεῖτε τοὺς οὕτω περιπατοῦντας καθὼς ἔχετε τύπον ἡμᾶς·

verses.restored: For many walk, of whom I often told you and now tell you weeping, as enemies of the cross of Messiah,

familiar.text: (For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ:

modern.text: For as I have often told you before, and now say again even with tears: Many live as enemies of the cross of Christ.

original.text: πολλοὶ γὰρ περιπατοῦσιν οὓς πολλάκις ἔλεγον ὑμῖν, νῦν δὲ καὶ κλαίων λέγω, τοὺς ἐχθροὺς τοῦ σταυροῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ,

verses.restored: whose completion is destruction, whose god is the belly, and whose glory is in their shame, those thinking earthly things.

familiar.text: Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.)

modern.text: Their end is destruction, their god is their belly, and their glory is in their shame. Their minds are set on earthly things.

original.text: ὧν τὸ τέλος ἀπώλεια, ὧν ὁ θεὸς ἡ κοιλία καὶ ἡ δόξα ἐν τῇ αἰσχύνῃ αὐτῶν, οἱ τὰ ἐπίγεια φρονοῦντες.

verses.restored: For our citizenship exists in heavens, from where also we eagerly await a savior/healer, Lord Jesus Messiah,

familiar.text: For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ:

modern.text: But our citizenship is in heaven, and we eagerly await a Savior from there, the Lord Jesus Christ,

original.text: ἡμῶν γὰρ τὸ πολίτευμα ἐν οὐρανοῖς ὑπάρχει, ἐξ οὗ καὶ σωτῆρα ἀπεκδεχόμεθα κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν,

verses.restored: who will transform the body of our humiliation to be conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working by which he is able even to subject all things to himself.

familiar.text: Who shall change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body, according to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself.

modern.text: who, by the power that enables Him to subject all things to Himself, will transform our lowly bodies to be like His glorious body.

original.text: ὃς μετασχηματίσει τὸ σῶμα τῆς ταπεινώσεως ⸀ἡμῶν σύμμορφον τῷ σώματι τῆς δόξης αὐτοῦ κατὰ τὴν ἐνέργειαν τοῦ δύνασθαι αὐτὸν καὶ ὑποτάξαι ⸀αὑτῷ τὰ πάντα.

translation_notes: Paul's sharp warning in 3:2 targets rival confidence-in-flesh pressure, not Jewish identity as contempt. His own Jewish credentials are named as real but relativized in Messiah.
Righteousness/justice through trust/faithfulness of Messiah preserves pistis Christou ambiguity.
The body is transformed, not discarded; 3:21 is embodied hope.
